evaluations.subject: census
evaluations.claim: Every member of the defined population is included.
evaluations.explanation: Useful when information about every member is genuinely required; complete coverage does not prevent measurement error.

evaluations.subject: census
evaluations.claim: Includes even very small subgroups of the population.
evaluations.explanation: There is no risk of a subgroup being absent merely because it was not sampled.

evaluations.subject: census
evaluations.claim: Measuring everyone can be expensive and time-consuming.
evaluations.explanation: The larger the population, the more resources may be needed.

evaluations.subject: census
evaluations.claim: Cannot be used when each test destroys the item being tested.
evaluations.explanation: Testing every manufactured safety harness to destruction would leave none to sell.

evaluations.subject: census
evaluations.claim: A large volume of data can be difficult to process.
evaluations.explanation: Full-population observations may require substantial handling and storage.

evaluations.subject: sample
evaluations.claim: Collecting a sample is usually quicker and cheaper than a census.
evaluations.explanation: Fewer observations need to be collected.

evaluations.subject: sample
evaluations.claim: Fewer members of the population need to respond.
evaluations.explanation: Especially useful where surveys take time.

evaluations.subject: sample
evaluations.claim: There are fewer observations to process.
evaluations.explanation: Reduces data-processing work.

evaluations.subject: sample
evaluations.claim: Different samples may produce different estimates.
evaluations.explanation: Sampling variation means conclusions are not guaranteed to be identical.

evaluations.subject: sample
evaluations.claim: A sample might omit an important small subgroup.
evaluations.explanation: This is particularly relevant when the subgroup itself is being studied.

evaluations.subject: sample
evaluations.claim: A poorly chosen sample can misrepresent the population.
evaluations.explanation: An incomplete frame or convenience selection may introduce systematic error.

evaluations.subject: simple-random
evaluations.claim: Randomly selected numbers remove deliberate interviewer choice from the selection stage.
evaluations.explanation: This reduces selection bias from personal preference but does not ensure perfect representativeness.

evaluations.subject: simple-random
evaluations.claim: Every possible sample of the chosen size has the same probability.
evaluations.explanation: The defining property of a simple random sample.

evaluations.subject: simple-random
evaluations.claim: Straightforward to carry out for a small, numbered population.
evaluations.explanation: A complete frame and random-number generator make implementation practical.

evaluations.subject: simple-random
evaluations.claim: A complete sampling frame is needed.
evaluations.explanation: An incomplete or outdated list can exclude eligible units.

evaluations.subject: simple-random
evaluations.claim: Can be cumbersome for a large, widely spread population.
evaluations.explanation: Obtaining the frame and contacting randomly selected units may be costly.

evaluations.subject: simple-random
evaluations.claim: Small subgroups may be underrepresented by chance.
evaluations.explanation: No fixed subgroup proportions are guaranteed in an ordinary simple random sample.

evaluations.subject: systematic
evaluations.claim: Once the interval is set, selection is quick and simple.
evaluations.explanation: Only one random starting point is needed.

evaluations.subject: systematic
evaluations.claim: Convenient for large ordered lists.
evaluations.explanation: Regular selection can be easier to administer than choosing many separate random numbers.

evaluations.subject: systematic
evaluations.claim: An ordered sampling frame is required.
evaluations.explanation: The method needs a list with defined positions.

evaluations.subject: systematic
evaluations.claim: A periodic pattern in the list can produce a distorted sample.
evaluations.explanation: For example, if every tenth entry belongs to a particular category, selecting every tenth unit can be unrepresentative.

evaluations.subject: stratified
evaluations.claim: Ensures each specified stratum has the intended proportional representation.
evaluations.explanation: Helpful when group proportions matter to the investigation.

evaluations.subject: stratified
evaluations.claim: Allows planned coverage of important population groups.
evaluations.explanation: Makes it less likely that an important group is missed by chance.

evaluations.subject: stratified
evaluations.claim: Population members must be classified into distinct strata.
evaluations.explanation: Classification can be difficult or costly if group information is incomplete.

evaluations.subject: stratified
evaluations.claim: Random selection is still needed within each stratum.
evaluations.explanation: The method inherits framing and practical difficulties of simple random selection.

evaluations.subject: quota
evaluations.claim: Chosen group proportions can be reflected in a relatively small sample.
evaluations.explanation: This only guarantees representation for the characteristics used to set quotas.

evaluations.subject: quota
evaluations.claim: No complete list of the population is required.
evaluations.explanation: People can be recruited directly into target groups.

evaluations.subject: quota
evaluations.claim: Recruitment is often quick, easy and inexpensive.
evaluations.explanation: No random selection from every group list is necessary.

evaluations.subject: quota
evaluations.claim: Specified groups can be included for comparison.
evaluations.explanation: Only those grouping characteristics are controlled.

evaluations.subject: quota
evaluations.claim: Non-random recruitment can introduce selection bias.
evaluations.explanation: Convenient or approachable people may be overrepresented within each quota.

evaluations.subject: quota
evaluations.claim: Defining and checking many groups can be costly or inaccurate.
evaluations.explanation: More characteristics create more group combinations and administrative burden.

evaluations.subject: quota
evaluations.claim: Refusals may not be recorded as non-responses.
evaluations.explanation: The replacement of non-respondents can hide participation problems.

evaluations.subject: opportunity
evaluations.claim: Easy to arrange with people already available.
evaluations.explanation: Does not require a full sampling frame.

evaluations.subject: opportunity
evaluations.claim: Usually inexpensive and fast to carry out.
evaluations.explanation: Convenient location and time reduce recruitment effort.

evaluations.subject: opportunity
evaluations.claim: People present in one place or time may not represent the wider population.
evaluations.explanation: E.g. morning shoppers may differ from evening shoppers.

evaluations.subject: opportunity
evaluations.claim: Who is approached may depend heavily on the researcher.
evaluations.explanation: Personal choice and willingness to respond can distort the sample.
